name: SIGNAL
tagline: Complex underneath, effortless on the surface.
summary: A consumer investing companion. Ask whether to hold a position over the next quarter and get an answer first: the stance, the confidence, three reasons, two risks, and what would change the call. Underneath, a quantitative score computed in code and a model-written bull and bear case are kept deliberately separate, and where they disagree the disagreement is shown rather than averaged away.
positioning: My one flagship independent project. It serves as the product I am building, the engineering portfolio I am judged on, the place coursework gets applied, and the subject of a public build log. One product, one codebase, one journey.
status_summary: The research engine, the evaluation suite and the daily export pipeline are built and running. The front end reads published runs for a watchlist of eight tickers. Predictions are logged but not yet scored against outcomes, so there is no accuracy claim yet.

business.target_customer: A retail investor who holds a handful of individual positions, reads some financial news, and wants a second opinion before changing a position. Not a day trader and not a professional analyst.
business.problem: Deciding whether to hold means reconciling valuation, momentum, risk, balance sheet, macro and the filings at once. Most consumer tools answer with one confident score and hide the uncertainty, so a user cannot tell when the tool is guessing.
business.value: An answer the user can interrogate: a number computed in code that no model can argue with, a stated case for and against, every claim marked sourced or not, and a visible flag when the quantitative view and the narrative view disagree.
business.competitors: Broker research pages, Seeking Alpha, Simply Wall St, Finviz, and the growing set of large-language-model stock chatbots. The nearest comparisons are the ones that show a scored breakdown; the gap is that few of them separate the model's reasoning from the number or expose disagreement.
monetization_hypotheses: A subscription for fresh research on arbitrary tickers, with the free tier limited to the published watchlist.
A paid tier for tracking a personal watchlist with alerts when a stance or a kill criterion changes.
One-off deep reports on a named company.
business.operating_costs: Today: effectively zero. Static hosting on GitHub Pages, free-tier market data behind a Cloudflare Worker, and free-tier models through OpenRouter. The first real cost appears when arbitrary tickers need a hosted API and paid model calls.
business.smallest_useful_mvp: What exists now plus a resolved track record: a user can ask about a covered company, see the stance with its reasoning, and see how previous calls actually turned out.
business.acquisition_idea: The build-in-public log itself, plus posting resolved calls once there is a track record worth showing. No paid acquisition until the product retains anyone.
business.disclaimer: Every revenue and market statement here is an untested hypothesis. SIGNAL has no users, no revenue, and no validated demand.

roadmap.name: Stage 1 — Ship
roadmap.detail: The engine, the evals and the export pipeline are done. What is missing before this is genuinely useful is a resolved track record: the prediction log records an entry price and a horizon end for every run, but nothing closes the loop against what actually happened.
roadmap.next: Resolve the logged predictions against realised prices and publish the calibration report the code already knows how to compute.

roadmap.name: Stage 2 — Validate
roadmap.goal: Get real users and watch what they actually do.
roadmap.detail: No users yet. The first question is whether anyone returns after one answer, and which part of the output they read.

roadmap.name: Stage 3 — Monetize
roadmap.detail: Only meaningful once something is retained. The natural paywall is fresh research for tickers outside the published watchlist, because that is also where the real cost sits.

roadmap.name: Stage 4 — Improve
roadmap.goal: Strengthen reliability, performance and usability on evidence.
roadmap.detail: Driven by what users and the resolved track record expose, not by what is technically interesting.

timeline.name: Product research
timeline.evidence: Design concept and interface prototype built out, kept verbatim in the repository's design reference.

timeline.name: Research engine built
timeline.evidence: Evidence, quant, bull, bear, synthesis and critic stages with a versioned score, a SQLite store and local tracing.

timeline.name: Evaluation suite
timeline.evidence: Thirteen eval cases bound by id to checks, including three proving the model cannot set the score.

timeline.name: Initial deployment
timeline.evidence: Static front end live on GitHub Pages with a scheduled weekday export committed back to the repository.

timeline.name: Resolved track record
timeline.evidence: 154 predictions logged across 15 tickers on a three-month horizon; none yet scored against outcomes.
